mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as low rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 9.0% (UNRATE) signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings from weak labor markets.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) below their 3-month moving averages signal weakening demand, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as revenue expectations deteriorate.
failure_condition: The joint decline condition (HOUST and RSAFS both below 3-month MA) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return association).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 12-month moving average), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative as supply chain disruptions dampen corporate profits and investor sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 12-month MA (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL year-over-year inflation rate above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as real rates rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as consumer spending expectations fall.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative return association).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level above 550 (HOUST > 550,000 units) is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns, as strong housing activity signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 550 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 90 (INDPRO < 90) signals supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market participants anticipate reduced output and higher input costs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
